$comment: MCP servers this factory depends on. Read by scripts/factory-mcp.mjs; nothing here is hardcoded in the script. This is a DECLARATION OF NEED, not a list of what a machine happens to have. A machine that does not configure one of these is not broken - `scope` skips it and says so, and `audit` still reports every server it actually runs. Change or delete this file to make the factory depend on a different set of servers, or on none at all (an empty list makes `scope` turn every configured server off for the project, which is a legitimate configuration).
why: Empty on purpose, and this used to name graft. Do not read the empty list as unfinished work. Three instruments said graft was generated once and never read: 1 graft tool call in 40,467 recorded tool calls (and that one in a project the factory never touched), 0 graft commands in PowerShell history, and 0 telemetry events in the 25 days between installation and removal. Its 1,437 cards in CLIProxyAPIPlus were built and last touched two seconds apart, then nothing for 17 days. It was real and good at one question - 'where is X used?', 98% smaller than reading the files whole - and useless at the question this work actually asks, 'what files exist here?': ls beat graft repo-map 317 bytes to 5,185 at 3,557 files, a gap that widens as a repo grows. glob was called 5,955 times out of 7,156 tool calls in the factory repo, 83%. You cannot save tokens on a 300-byte operation. So the factory now depends on no MCP server at all. A project enables one explicitly with `factory mcp scope --allow <name>` when a feature needs it, and `factory mcp audit` reports whatever is actually configured.
